IMPLEMENTATION + VALIDATION

What you can inspect.
What still needs setup.

Implemented locally

Agent skill registry

Three project-owned skills document the tools, supported test networks, limits and human review required for each workflow. The registry is served by the local workspace and exposed as an MCP resource.

A project registry, not an official global skills listing or installation.

Local developer preview

Keyless MCP connection

The preview exposes 15 tools over local stdio. Your MCP client supplies the model. The connector itself needs no model-provider API key; it uses the workspace’s existing connection.

The 15-tool preview is separate from the prepared connector release. Public package and Registry publication are pending.

Flow implemented · Internal proof

Arc tMGAS requests and receipts

An agent quotes an exact test-USDC amount, creates one stable purchase request and returns its owner review. MetaMask separately approves the allowance and purchase. The agent reads the same request for verified delivery evidence.

The internal 1 test USDC → 100 tMGAS conversion is verified. The buyer pays network fees; Arc tokens remain separate from Base service credits.

Optional · Private and local

OpenAI copilot

A separate local chat uses the operator’s configured OpenAI connection. It has Arc purchase and read-only Solana modes, with three tools per mode: six capabilities. The provider connection and Solana balance/setup flow are verified through the browser. The separate MCP preview still exposes 15 tools.

The copilot cannot sign, submit wallet transactions, mint or trade. Provider credentials are entered in the local setup form, never agent chat.

Read-only flow verified

Solana Devnet readiness

A MetaMask Solana wallet connection and the browser-to-model balance/setup flow have been verified. Three read-only tools check configuration readiness, missing setup steps and balances for the selected public Solana address. This mode does not use the Arc EVM buyer.

The current local setup has no configured SPL mint or sponsor. Sponsored execution awaits that setup, sponsor funding and a verified transaction.

In development

One shared gas account

Canonical Base tMGAS funds one operator-managed prepaid service account. Read-only backtest and reconciliation services use bounded prices and ledger receipts. Funded sponsors are the proposed route to native fees across supported networks.

Shared-credit native-gas dispatch remains disabled on all five test networks. Wallet connection and readiness checks are not execution proof.

Arc tMGAS purchase

FOR DEVELOPERS WITH WORKSPACE ACCESS

Bring your own client.
Keep approval with you.

  1. Start the local workspace

    Use the project’s local operator instructions and Node.js 22 or later. The public website repository contains this site and research downloads; it does not contain the private payment backend or an installable agent service.

  2. Connect the preview through stdio

    In the local Agents section, copy the generated MCP configuration into your own MCP-compatible client. Use its separate command and arguments fields. A web page URL is not the stdio MCP connection.

  3. Discover, then request

    List the connector’s actual tools and read the relevant registry skill. For an Arc token purchase, quote the exact amount, keep one request key and return the review page to the owner. A quote or request does not authorize spending.

  4. Review in MetaMask, then inspect evidence

    The owner approves the exact allowance and purchase separately. Poll the original request ID. Report success only when the state is confirmed and its receipt is verified. An uncertain submission keeps its existing intent; it is not automatically resent.

Use Solana mode: select Solana Devnet in the local copilot, choose the public Solana address to inspect, then ask for its balances or missing setup steps. The three tools are status, balances and setup checklist. This mode only reads; it cannot prepare, sign or send a transaction.

◈

One token vision. Explicit accounting today.

Arc USDC conversion, Circle Facilitator checkout and Base-funded service credits are separate flows. Arc native USDC uses 18 decimals; its ERC-20 interface uses six and represents the same balance. The Arc tMGAS purchase has no 10% sale markup; service pricing and network fees are disclosed separately.

KEEP THE CLAIMS CHECKABLE

Evidence and next steps.

The verified internal Arc testnet purchase exchanged 1 test USDC for 100 tMGAS. Its recorded result was 10,000 tMGAS total supply, 9,900 remaining converter inventory and zero residual buyer allowances. These are internal test results, not adoption or revenue.

Next gates include an owner-signed Circle Facilitator settlement proof, configured Solana sponsorship, a funded shared-gas dispatch pilot and independent review before production use. No mainnet, bridge, redemption, public hosted execution or Circle partnership is claimed.
